## Question

The Long-Term Evolution Experiment provides genome sequences from *Escherichia coli* sampled over 50,000 generations [@tenaillon2016]. How many mutations distinguish these clones, and how sensitive are the counts to a minimum-depth filter? As a first step, this report examines the paired sequence reads used to call those variants.

## Data

```{python}
#| tags: [parameters]
max_reads = 10000
```

```{python}
#| label: setup
from pathlib import Path
import sys

import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown, display
from scripts.fastq_stats import quality_by_position, summarize

samples = pd.read_csv("metadata/samples.tsv", sep="\t", keep_default_na=False)
samples = samples.sort_values("generation")
fastq_files = samples["fastq_1"].tolist() + samples["fastq_2"].tolist()
generations = ", ".join(f"{g:,}" for g in samples["generation"])


def show_table(frame):
    # Emit a Markdown table so Quarto can render it in both HTML and PDF.
    rows = [frame.columns, ["---"] * len(frame.columns), *frame.itertuples(index=False, name=None)]
    display(Markdown("\n".join("| " + " | ".join(map(str, row)) + " |" for row in rows)))
```

The Data Carpentry teaching subset [@dc_data] contains paired reads from `{python} len(samples)` Ara-3 clones sampled at generations `{python} generations` (@tbl-samples). In the sample sheet, `None` is a recorded mutator status and `unknown` denotes an undetermined citrate-use phenotype.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-samples
#| tbl-cap: "LTEE clones in generation order. Sample identifiers are SRA runs."
show_table(samples[["sample", "strain", "generation", "mutator", "cit"]])
```

## Reads

@tbl-reads counts every record in each FASTQ file. The parameter limits the length, GC and base-quality summaries to the first `{python} f'{max_reads:,}'` reads per file. GC is the percentage of sampled bases that are G or C. Mean Q is the arithmetic mean of their Phred+33 scores. Each file identifier below omits the shared suffix `.trim.sub.fastq`.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-reads
#| tbl-cap: "Full read counts and prefix summaries by run and mate (1 or 2)."
reads = pd.DataFrame([summarize(path, max_reads) for path in sorted(fastq_files)])
read_table = pd.DataFrame({
    "File": reads["file"].str.removesuffix(".trim.sub.fastq"),
    "Reads": reads["reads"].map("{:,}".format),
    "Mean length (bp)": reads["mean_length"].map("{:.1f}".format),
    "GC (%)": reads["gc_percent"].map("{:.1f}".format),
    "Mean Q": reads["mean_quality"].map("{:.1f}".format),
})
show_table(read_table)
```

```{python}
#| label: paired-counts
#| include: false
counts = reads.set_index("file")["reads"]
pairs = {}
for row in samples.itertuples(index=False):
    r1, r2 = (counts[Path(path).name] for path in (row.fastq_1, row.fastq_2))
    if r1 != r2:
        raise ValueError(f"Mates have different record counts for {row.sample}")
    pairs[row.sample] = r1
if len(set(pairs.values())) == 1:
    pair_text = f"{next(iter(pairs.values())):,} read pairs per clone"
else:
    pair_text = ", ".join(f"{count:,} read pairs for {run}" for run, count in pairs.items())
n_sampled = reads["reads"].clip(upper=max_reads)
mean_length = (reads["mean_length"] * n_sampled).sum() / n_sampled.sum()
```

The paired files contain `{python} pair_text`. Across the sampled reads, the mean length after trimming is `{python} f'{mean_length:.1f}'` bases.

## Quality along the read

```{python}
#| label: fig-quality
#| fig-cap: "Mean base quality by position in the sampled prefix of each FASTQ file. Colour identifies the clone and line style identifies the mate."
#| fig-alt: "Six quality profiles, one solid line for read 1 and one dashed line for read 2 of each clone. The horizontal axis is position from the start of a read; the vertical axis is mean Phred score among reads that reach that position. The text below gives the observed ranges at the two ends of the shared interval."
profiles = {}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.3))
for row, color in zip(samples.itertuples(index=False), ["#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73"]):
    for mate, path, style in [(1, row.fastq_1, "-"), (2, row.fastq_2, "--")]:
        q = quality_by_position(path, max_reads)
        profiles[(row.sample, mate)] = q
        ax.plot(q.index, q, color=color, linestyle=style, linewidth=1.4,
                label=f"{row.sample} R{mate}")
ax.set(xlabel="Position in read (bases)", ylabel="Mean Phred score")
ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
ax.legend(ncol=3, fontsize=8, frameon=False, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.16))
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: quality-ranges
#| include: false
last_shared = min(q.index[-1] for q in profiles.values())

def score_range(pos):
    values = [q.loc[pos] for q in profiles.values()]
    return f"{min(values):.1f}–{max(values):.1f}"
```

Across the six profiles in @fig-quality, the mean scores span `{python} score_range(1)` at base 1 and `{python} score_range(last_shared)` at base `{python} last_shared`, the last position shared by all profiles. Each point averages only reads long enough to contribute a base at that position.
